answer: Wattlyst publishes two original datasets for Pakistan, each refreshed monthly with a chart, its method and a free CSV under CC BY: the Bill Index, the bill at every step of units for every DISCO, and the Solar Price Tracker, dated prices of panels, systems, inverters and batteries from dealer and installer lists.

p: The [[bill-index|Pakistan Electricity Bill Index]] shows what a month's bill should be for a given number of units, protected and unprotected, with the month's FPA. Use it to check a bill or compare months; the [[F1|electricity bill calculator]] works out your own bill.

The [[solar-price-tracker|Pakistan Solar Price Tracker]] records panel, system, inverter and battery prices with their sources and dates. Use it to judge a quote with the [[N3|solar quote checker]], or to see how prices moved before you buy.

Both datasets are free to reuse with credit to Wattlyst and a link to the page. Journalists and researchers can download the CSV from each page; the method section on each page explains how the figures are built and where they come from.

faq.q: How often is the data updated?
faq.a: Every month. Each page shows the date its data was last checked, and the CSV download carries the same figures as the tables.

faq.q: Can I use the data in my article?
faq.a: Yes, under the Creative Commons Attribution licence: credit Wattlyst and link to the page you took the figures from.

faq.q: Where do the numbers come from?
faq.a: The Bill Index runs the NEPRA domestic tariff through the same engine as the bill calculators. The Solar Price Tracker collects dated dealer and installer price lists and news reports, each listed under Sources on the page.

faq.q: Is the Bill Index an official bill?
faq.a: No. It is an estimate from the notified tariff for a stated sanctioned load. Your own bill also carries arrears, meter rent or tax that the index leaves out; the [[N1|overbilling check]] helps with a bill that looks wrong.
